resolved.meaning: Family delta disappeared; this alone is not a bug-fix or quality claim.

component.meaning: Internal component consumes supplied findings/views/AST/budgets or observes one suboperation. A whole-engine scan of captured text is not the same function call.

refused.meaning: Rejected path/byte limits are excluded from detector agreement and successful-negative counts.

taxonomy.meaning: A documented counterpart is actually present at the same single input file. Related signals are not proof of equivalent source-to-sink inference, severity or verdict.

type_context.meaning: Upstream explicit Python file_type/AST is supplied for a non-Python artifact name. Raw replay does not inject that parser/type fact.

known_gap.meaning: Individually inspected Bash fetch-to-execution input still lacks SC2: constructed fetch URL or process substitution. This is retained as a detector gap, not accepted as harmless or counted as a successful negative.

python.meaning: Resolved same-file bounded IR with ordered overwrites, explicit imports, isolated method receivers and selected calls. Selected literal/aliased containers, vararg forwarding, comprehensions and direct global/nonlocal effects are modeled. No import invention, union of overwritten sources, backwards cyclic fixpoint or arbitrary cross-method invocation-order invention. Unsupported/budget evidence is retained separately.

shell_truth.meaning: Selected concrete unsafe arguments, defaults and workload declarations; standalone --force/--skip-validation and unrelated chained commands are insufficient. Python uses resolved calls and bounded evaluation; unsupported grammar is not completion. Shell quotes, glob expansion, statements and octal bits retain their distinct meanings.

credential.meaning: Credential/privilege actions or supported capability declarations. Bare credential-store names, OAuth nouns/lifecycle/persistence, /etc/passwd identity maps, ignore-file entries and syntactic path construction are not automatically secret access. Concrete keyring reads/exports, bound token disclosure and supported sensitive file reads are covered. No blanket documentation exemption.

network.meaning: Selected network/body/environment/filesystem/SSRF signals; command-local ownership, source types and concrete destinations matter. Separate curl and --data sentences, arbitrary home enumeration and host-language continuations are not proven network transfers. Literal signals still include data/examples and require review.

prompt.meaning: Bounded raw/Unicode/reconstructed instruction signals. Code identifier boundaries and narrow formatting headings differ from extraction; explicit privileged requests and heading-as-command framing remain signals. Strict known emoji/tag exemptions, bounded marker grammar and layout thresholds intentionally differ from upstream prepared views and contextual heuristics.

agency.meaning: Concrete wildcard/autonomy/scope/resource/provider signals, not every including-but-not-limited-to clause or licence mutation. Model frontmatter requires the YAML parser. Bare CLI names/model-like data and ordinary configuration prose do not establish external provider selection.

output.meaning: Selected execution/output crossings and unbounded-output signals. Python checks execution arguments rather than metadata strings. A narrowly recognized JS regexp.exec is excluded; ambiguous JS stays a review signal. General SQL/type inference and all web-framework sinks are outside this bounded detector.

memory.meaning: Selected memory/state adoption and repetition signals with independent raw-byte evidence. Repeated data values may receive a medium review signal; sample/example labels do not grant trust. Hardware/state vocabulary, paragraph ownership and thresholds differ from upstream context filtering.

agent.meaning: Selected self-modification/persistence/snooping/refusal actions. Actual cp/mv/install destinations and command-word boundaries matter; mkdir is not dir and installation is not enumeration. Bare peer-SKILL paths, inferred remote repository identity and all prose variants are not equivalent to an observed read. Literal review signals can also occur in examples.

supply.meaning: Offline selected source/config/encoding/dependency/integrity checks. Source strings, package-name neighbours, decoding and execution are distinct signals; decoded children are independently inspected. Bounded shell config generation is not a POSIX interpreter: Bash syntax projection observes functions/branches/loops/case, selected tee outputs and generated package TOML/YAML/XML. Dynamic command effects, arbitrary outputs and execution semantics remain incomplete. Incomplete scope never becomes an allow.

integrity.meaning: Scout retains raw/derived namespace and completeness evidence with its own binary/archive/text limits. Runtime views, opaque references, UTF-16/legacy encodings, excluded paths, canonical magic and deadline-injected state differ. Concealment signals are review heuristics, not proof that text is malicious.

hooks.meaning: Namespace-scoped hook/permission evidence with strict closed upload proof. Exotic curl-only URL normalization, malformed/control-bearing headers and injected workflow limits do not establish the same closed proof. Hook capability/incomplete inspection remains independently reported.

permissions.meaning: Nearest captured skill/plugin namespace and lexical capability hints. Missing declarations use LP3; wildcard declarations use LP2. Permission strings are not host enforcement; arbitrary scoped allowed-tools strings do not prove coverage of all code capabilities.

updates.meaning: Prior/current manifest comparison is a separate Scout API; a raw current-only replay cannot provide history. Mutable execution has dedicated Scout checks. A wildcard in a skill own version field alone is not an unpinned dependency.

tools.meaning: Static tool metadata checks plus optional explicitly configured semantic description/behavior review. Provider responses, injected model budgets and prior runtime state are not raw-file input. No live model is enabled by this offline replay.

triggers.meaning: Parsed structural trigger checks use NV-TR*M; older literal TR* signals remain separately identified. A missing structural family ID is not proof that activation or coverage was established.

deserialization.meaning: Selected parsed and literal deserialization capabilities; supported Python source-to-sink observations are separate. No arbitrary dynamic type or cross-file inference.

yara.meaning: Pinned bundled YARA-X rules and explicit trusted ExtraRules. Custom test rule directories, fake severity/category/cache/load failures and injected match caps are additional operator/runtime inputs, not bytes of the scanned files. Built-in prompt prohibitions and ransomware instances are post-filtered without suppressing later affirmative evidence.

offline_service.meaning: OSV lookup is explicitly configured and network-disabled by default. Upstream fake lookup responses, locked-version maps, service failures and fallback databases are not replayed as file contents; they are covered by Scout service/API tests, not asserted equal here.
